source_evidence: For accepted orders the warehouse picks the parts, packs the order and books a carrier.
problem: The warehouse department is classified as an automated authority instead of a human organisational performer.
correction: Change Lane_warehouse laneMeta authority from "authority" to "sovereignty".

source_evidence:
The warehouse also does quality inspection and labelling for each order, but nobody could
say whether those happen before or after packing, or in which order relative to each other.

map_evidence.quote: <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="pick-parts--quality-inspection" sourceRef="pick-parts" targetRef="quality-inspection" /><bpmn:sequenceFlow id="quality-inspection--pack-order" sourceRef="quality-inspection" targetRef="pack-order" />

problem: The map imposes quality inspection between picking and packing despite the explicitly unknown inspection order.
correction: Remove both sequence flows through quality-inspection and their incoming/outgoing references, restore a direct pick-parts to pack-order flow, and leave quality-inspection unconnected with an annotation declaring its unknown order relative to packing and labelling.

map_evidence.quote: <bpmn:task id="send-payment-reminder" name="Send payment reminder"><bpmn:documentation>source: "The ERP sends a payment reminder after seven days."</bpmn:documentation>

problem: The map adds an ERP payment-reminder step after invoicing and supports it with a fabricated source quotation.
correction: Remove send-payment-reminder, its documentation, lane reference and incident flows; connect generate-and-send-invoice directly to accepted-order-fulfilled and update the corresponding incoming/outgoing references.
